messages:
sophia_customer: Hi team, since ~09:10 our Private control plane calls from our VPC to Redwood are failing with an mTLS handshake error. App logs show: 

  ERROR: handshake failure: short record 
  tls: oversized record received with length 20527

We haven't changed certs. It works from some subnets but not others. Any quick checks?

eric_support: Sorry to hear that — can you paste the exact curl / openssl output from one of the failing hosts? Also which region and whether you're going via a NAT/egress appliance?

sophia_customer: region: us-west-2. Failing hosts are behind our legacy NAT appliance (vendor: AcmeEdge). Working hosts are in a different AZ using AWS NAT Gateway. From a failing host:

  $ openssl s_client -connect control.redwood.example.com:443 -servername control.redwood.example.com -msg -tls1_3
  <<< TLS 1.3, ClientHello, length=5120
  read:errno=104

curl shows: "schannel: next InitializeSecurityContext failed: SEC_E_ILLEGAL_MESSAGE (0x80090326) - The message received was unexpected or badly formatted."

eric_support: interesting — oversized record / short record often points at MTU/fragmentation or a TCP proxy mangling TLS records. Can you run a tcpdump on the failing host capturing the initial ClientHello and the server response? Filter for port 443 and paste the hex or pcap?

kevin_oncall: adding context: our control plane expects unmodified TLS passthrough; some NGFWs terminate or modify TLS leading to those errors. Also if ClientHello is fragmented across multiple TCP segments and the middlebox doesn't handle it, handshakes break for TLS1.3 because of larger ClientHello (keyshares + extensions).

sophia_customer: attaching a short tcpdump excerpt (base64 pcap): [omitted for slack]. I also tried lowering MTU on host to 1400 and the handshake succeeds.

eric_support: aha — MTU change success is a strong sign. Can you confirm the path MTU and whether the AcmeEdge box performs MSS clamping or TCP segmentation offload manipulation?

maria_netops: pinging in — our appliance does TCP optimization and sometimes does TLS inspection. Customer says they didn't configure inspection, but firmware auto-inspects on certain traffic patterns. SophIa, can you check the appliance logs (AcmeEdge px logs) for TLS/SSL inspection triggers?

sophia_customer: checking now — log shows: "SSL_Inspection: client_hello_fragmented, action=inspect" at the times of the failed handshakes. We can toggle inspection but it's a managed device and takes a day to change policy.

eric_support: two paths for remediation: short term — force MSS clamping or lower MTU on the box so ClientHello isn't fragmented, or bypass the appliance for control plane IPs (egress allowlist). Long term — update appliance firmware/config to preserve TLS passthrough or disable inspection for our control plane ranges.

kevin_oncall: for immediate mitigation we can provide the control plane IPs and FQDNs to allowlist: 
  - 54.172.23.11/32
  - 54.172.23.12/32
  - control.redwood.example.com (SNI must be preserved)

sophia_customer: can you confirm ports? we allow 443 only, right?

eric_support: correct, TCP/443 and keep SNI intact. Also ensure the appliance doesn't rewrite TLS extension order or strip keyshare extensions. If you must keep the appliance in path, try enabling "TLS passthrough" mode in AcmeEdge or disable SSL inspection for those IPs.

maria_netops: additional suggestion — disable large offload features (GSO/TSO/LRO) on host NICs as a workaround. Commands we recommend on linux:

  sudo ethtool -K eth0 tso off gso off gro off

That reduces segmentation that can cause middleboxes to see odd record boundaries.

sophia_customer: tried ethtool toggles on one host; handshake still failed until we lowered MTU on appliance path. But disabling offloads is a helpful step, thanks.

eric_support: good data. We'll mark this as "mtls-fragmentation-egress" and escalate to our networking team to confirm whether control plane should accept fragmented ClientHello (it should) or whether we need to present a compatibility note for customers behind legacy middleboxes.

kevin_oncall: tagging deploy-bot:deploy 2016501300 — was there any infra change around 09:00 that could exacerbate this?

deploy-bot: deploy log: no control-plane deploys between 08:45-09:30. No certificate rotations recorded.

eric_support: next steps for the customer — (1) add control plane IPs to appliance bypass/allowlist for TCP/443 (SNI preserved) as the fastest fix, (2) schedule firmware update or policy change on AcmeEdge to disable SSL inspection for these flows, (3) enable MSS clamping on the appliance or enforce MTU 1400 on the path, (4) optionally disable NIC offloads as emergency host-side workaround.

sophia_customer: we'll push an allowlist change and test. Appreciate the quick help. If allowlist works we'll follow up about firmware change and permanent solution. :thumbsup:

eric_support: thanks, please post results here and we'll keep the thread open until green. If allowlist doesn't fix it send the pcap and we'll coordinate a packet-for-packet trace with our NOC.

sophia_customer: allowlist applied, tests pass from previously failing hosts. Latency looks normal and no handshake errors in logs. Closing this incident for now, will re-open if anything else crops up.

eric_support: great to hear — closing on our side too, filing a short KB ticket for customers behind legacy NAT/NGFWs: "mTLS handshake failures with large ClientHello due to fragmentation/inspection; recommend allowlist or MTU/MSS fixes."

kevin_oncall: adding KB tag and assigning to netops for follow-up next sprint. :white_check_mark:
